speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to begin our assessment, can you describe exactly how your balance and coordination have changed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like significant ataxia. Can you tell me if you have any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs, or if you've noticed any vision changes like double vision or blurred sight?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab for a year, combined with your new onset of gait and limb ataxia, this presentation is highly suspicious for PML, an opportunistic infection of the central nervous system. I need to confirm the neurological status and look for other signs like vision changes or cognitive decline.
